content: GPLD1, or glycosylphosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase D1, is an enzyme encoded by the GPLD1 gene in humans. This enzyme plays a critical role in the metabolism of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchors, which are glycolipids that tether many proteins to the extracellular surface of eukaryotic plasma membranes. GPI anchors are particularly abundant on various blood cells. The protein encoded by the GPLD1 gene functions as a GPI-degrading enzyme. Specifically, it hydrolyzes the inositol phosphate linkage within GPI-anchored proteins. This enzymatic activity results in the release of the attached proteins from the plasma membrane, effectively cleaving their connection to the cell surface. In terms of molecular interactions, GPLD1 has been demonstrated to interact with apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) and apolipoprotein A4 (ApoA4), which are key components of lipid metabolism and transport. These interactions suggest a potential role for GPLD1 in lipid-related processes and cellular signaling pathways.
